newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Monday:

* Microsoft, Intel and Compaq said they would set the standards for the new digital era, but even others in the personal computer business have failed to lend support and the three-company front seems to be disuniting.

* Cellularvision has persuaded 14,000 New York City customers to install its TV receivers, but the company has been unable to expand past New York due to a dispute with other companies that laid claim to its slice of the airwaves.

* Some Knight-Ridder editors are irritated by the fact that the company is taking the control of its foreign bureaus away from its four big papers and placing the reporters under the direction of a single Washington desk.
* The current practice of assigning Internet addresses is being investigated by the U.S. Justice Department to determine if the control amounts to violation of antitrust laws.
* British newspapers are contending with some of the toughest libel laws in the world.
* Many newspaper publishers are embracing the internet.
* Several web sites allow comsumers to find the credit cards best suited to them.
* Talks between union leaders and British Airways broke down, setting the stage for a three-day flight attendant strike.
* Video piracy is thriving in the U.S.
* Since Hitachi introduced its Skyline mainframe, large companies have been buying the machines as fast as the company can make them.
* The publishing industry is struggling with record-breaking returns of unsold copies.
* Internet entrepreneurs are trying to find out how to make money from those who enjoy virtual combat games.
